blogs.title: The 1.58-Bit Revolution: How AI Models Are Shrinking Without Losing Smarts
blogs.description: Explore the groundbreaking concept of BitNet b1.58, a new type of Large Language Model where every parameter is simplified to just three values (-1, 0, or 1). This post breaks down how reducing model precision from standard 16-bit to '1.58-bit' allows AI to match the intelligence of massive models while using a fraction of the memory and energy.

blogs.title: Green AI: Why the Future of Large Language Models Runs on Integer Addition
blogs.description: Dive into the environmental and economic impact of the new era of 1-bit LLMs. We explain how replacing complex floating-point multiplication with simple integer addition slashes energy consumption by over 70x for matrix operations, making it possible to run powerful AI on smaller hardware and significantly reducing the carbon footprint of generative AI.

blogs.title: From Data Centers to Your Pocket: Bringing 70B Models to Mobile Devices
blogs.description: Discover how BitNet b1.58 is changing the deployment landscape for AI. This post discusses how the drastic reduction in memory footprint and latency enables massive models (like a 70B parameter version) to run efficiently on edge devices, smartphones, and CPUs, opening the door for high-performance AI applications that were previously impossible outside of supercomputers.

blogs.title: The New Scaling Law: Why Smaller Bit-Width Means Bigger Performance
blogs.description: Challenge your assumptions about model size and performance. We analyze the surprising results showing that a smaller 1.58-bit model can outperform a larger full-precision model in speed and efficiency while maintaining equal accuracy. Learn about the new 'scaling law' where efficiency gains allow us to train larger, smarter models for the same cost.
